A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UFT research work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original fine-tuning experiments, success rates, inference times, and sensitivity analyses on Countdown and Game-of-24.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds GA/RepNoise comparisons and AMC-12 evaluation results.

M1.justification: The proposed UFT procedure remains unchanged: extract reasoning paths, separate correct and failed examples, and combine NLL with an auxiliary unlikelihood loss. Equations 1–6 and Algorithm 1 retain the same operations. The added alternative losses are evaluated comparators.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds training on 38k numerical-answer problems selected from OpenThoughts-114k-math and evaluation on AMC-12 2023 and 2024. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained Countdown and Game-of-24 arithmetic puzzles to competition mathematics.

E2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds evaluated Gradient Ascent and RepNoise alternatives on Game-of-24, with comparisons in Tables 7–8. GA was discussed but lacked reported performance comparisons in v3; RepNoise is newly introduced. Existing SFT, SimPO, and CPO-SimPO comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The existing puzzle protocols are retained. Appendix E introduces a distinct protocol using 38k training problems, two epochs, 2048-token contexts, final-answer verification with math-verify, and pass@1 estimated from 32 paths per problem. Appendix B.3 also introduces controlled alternative-loss experiments with specified coefficients and learning-rate sweeps.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds loss-substitution experiments and learning-rate/data-source sensitivity analyses for GA and RepNoise. These test whether the reported search-retention behavior extends to other forgetting objectives, including RepNoise's complete search-performance collapse. The original sensitivity plots remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 newly report Welch's t-test significance at p < 0.05, and Section 5.2 discusses seven significant UFT results and limited statistical power. The existing three- and four-seed summaries are retained; no increase in runs for those experiments is established.

E6.justification: Original table values and plotted results are retained, while Tables 7–9 add substantial new results. Table 8 reports zero ToT/RAP success for RepNoise across tested learning rates. Table 9 reports closely matched AMC performance among SFT, CPO-SimPO, and UFT, including 61.5% versus 61.6% for SFT versus UFT on AMC 2023 with Qwen2.5-Math 7B.

T1.justification: The existing UFT derivations remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds the formal RepNoise objective in Equation 11; Equation 10 restates GA's objective already present in v3's footnote 4. As printed, Equation 11 applies an outer logarithm to averaged log-probabilities, creating a nonpositive-argument domain problem.

C1.justification: V4 narrows the conclusion's stated application from mathematical reasoning to arithmetic puzzle domains and distinguishes the three-phase pipeline from its UFT objective. The three headline contributions concerning data quality, unpaired forgetting, and learning rate retain their substance and numerical claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds substantive applicability limits: correct final answers need not imply correct reasoning, and general-math data noise, differences across competition years, and limited training may constrain transfer. Appendix B.3 adds explanations linking RepNoise's search collapse to aggressive loss weighting and disruption of internal representations.

D1.justification: The new appendices document GA/RepNoise loss coefficients, math-data curation, answer verification, prompting, and training resources, including approximately 15 hours on eight A100 GPUs for the 7B math experiments. Existing puzzle implementation details and the code-access location are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations and discussion of inference-tree preference learning, concurrent reasoning-model unlearning, additional safety-oriented unlearning methods, and the new math-data sources. Section 2 retains the original positioning around unpaired, reference-free learning; existing Chen references merely receive different year suffixes.

P1.justification: V4 makes limited wording corrections, refines arithmetic-puzzle terminology, retitles Algorithm 1, and expands the conclusion with future work. Existing model-specific appendix results are consolidated into B.2, followed by new B.3 and Appendix E; the main narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: V4 adds Tables 7–9 and adds row-wise bolding, significance stars, and explanatory captions to Tables 2–3. Publication headers, colored links, and page reflow change the layout. All seven figures retain their original graphics.

improvement.justification: V4 adds useful direct unlearning comparisons and tests transfer to AMC, where it explicitly reports no clear UFT advantage over SFT/CPO-SimPO. Together with significance testing, this improves the empirical support and clarification of applicability limits. The net gain is limited by the few seeds, incompletely specified significance comparisons, and the domain error in the new RepNoise equation.
